verses.1: Then, O King, the mighty-armed Ravana, wandering on the earth, reached the Himalayan forest and roamed there.
verses.2: There he indeed saw a maiden, wearing a black deer-skin and matted hair, engaged in ascetic practices, shining like a goddess.
verses.3: Having seen that beautiful maiden observing great vows, he, whose mind was overcome by the delusion of desire, asked her as if with a smile.
verses.4: O gentle lady, what is this conduct of yours, which is contrary to your youth, for such actions are indeed not suitable for your beauty.
verses.5: O timid one, your incomparable beauty, which incites desire and madness in men, is not suitable for ascetic practices, for this is indeed a well-established conclusion.
verses.6: O gentle lady, whose are you, and what is this activity; O beautiful-faced one, who is your husband, for the man by whom you are enjoyed, O timid one, is indeed fortunate on this earth.
verses.7: Tell me everything, who am asking, for what reason is this exertion; thus spoken to by Ravana, that glorious maiden then replied.
verses.8: My father is Kushadhvaja, a Brahmarshi of immeasurable splendor, the glorious son of Brihaspati, and equal to Brihaspati in intellect.
verses.9: While my great-souled father was constantly engaged in the study of the Vedas, I was born as a daughter, manifested from his speech, and was known by the name Vedavati.
verses.10: Then, gods along with Gandharvas, Yakshas, Rakshasas, and Pannagas, all went to my father and sought my hand in marriage.
verses.11: But that father of mine did not give me to them, O best of Rakshasas; I will now tell you the reason for that, O night-wanderer, so listen.
verses.12: My father indeed desired Vishnu, the lord of gods and the lord of the three worlds, to be his son-in-law, and therefore he would not give me to anyone else.
verses.13: But upon hearing that my father desired to give me to Vishnu, the king of Daityas named Dambhu, who was proud of his strength, became enraged.
verses.14: My father, while sleeping at night, was killed by that wicked one.
verses.15: Then, my distressed mother, that noble lady, embraced my father's body and entered the fire.
verses.16: Then, I bear in my heart the true desire of my father towards Narayana, vowing to fulfill it.
verses.17: Thus, having undertaken this vow, I perform great austerity, and all this has been told to you by me, O best of Rakshasas.
verses.18: Narayana is my husband, and no one else is superior to Purushottama; I undertake a severe vow with the desire to obtain Narayana, and now that you are known to me, O king, O delight of Pulastya, you may go.
verses.19: I know all that indeed exists in the three worlds through my ascetic power.
verses.20: Afflicted by the arrows of Kama, Ravana descended from the top of his aerial car and spoke again to that maiden of great vows.
verses.21: O beautiful-hipped one, you are arrogant to have such a mind; O deer-eyed one, the accumulation of merit shines only for the aged.
verses.22: O most beautiful in the three worlds and O timid one, you who are endowed with all virtues ought not to speak such a thing, for your youth is passing away.
verses.23: O auspicious one, I am known as Dashagriva, the lord of Lanka; become my wife and enjoy pleasures as you please.
verses.24: Ravana asks Vedavati who this Vishnu is, whom she speaks of, and what he possesses in terms of valor, penance, enjoyment, and strength.
verses.25: Ravana declares to Vedavati that the one she desires is not equal to him.
verses.26: After Ravana had spoken thus, Vedavati then replied to him.
verses.27: Vedavati, the maiden, told the night-wanderer Ravana, "No, not so!" and asked, "O king of Rakshasas, who else among intelligent beings, besides you, would disrespect Vishnu, the lord of the three worlds, who is worshipped by all?"
verses.28: When Vedavati had spoken thus to him there, the night-wanderer Ravana then touched the maiden's hair with the tip of his hand.
verses.29: Then, enraged Vedavati cut off her hair with her hand, which, having transformed into a sword, severed her locks.
verses.30: Burning with rage as if to consume the night-wanderer, she, resolved to die, kindled a fire and spoke.
verses.31: O ignoble one, since I have been molested by you, I no longer desire to live, O Rakshasa; therefore, I shall enter the fire before your very eyes.
verses.32: Because I have been molested by your evil self in this forest, I shall indeed be born again for the sole purpose of your destruction.
verses.33: Indeed, it is not possible for a woman to kill a man of evil resolve, and if I were to utter a curse upon you, my accumulated penance would be lost.
verses.34: If I have indeed performed any good deeds, given charity, or offered sacrifices, then may I be born as the virtuous, womb-born daughter of a righteous man.
verses.35: Having spoken thus, she entered the blazing fire, and simultaneously, a divine shower of flowers fell from the sky all around.
verses.36: She emerged again from a lotus, radiant like a lotus, and from that lotus, she was again taken by that demon as before.
verses.37: Having seized the maiden, who shone like the heart of a lotus, the demon went to his own house, and Ravana then showed her to his minister.
verses.38: The physiognomist, having observed her, spoke to Ravana, saying, "This beautiful-hipped maiden, staying in your house, is indeed destined for your destruction."
verses.39: O Rama, having heard this, Ravana threw her into the water, and she, having reached the earth, indeed went into the middle of a sacrificial ground.
verses.40: O Lord, O mighty-armed one, she, having again arisen, drawn out by the ploughshare of King Janaka, is this daughter born to King Janaka, your wife, for you are indeed the eternal Vishnu.
verses.41: Previously, that mountain-like enemy, filled with anger, was thus killed by her, having resorted to your superhuman prowess.
verses.42: Thus, this highly fortunate one will again be born among mortals, in a field drawn out by the ploughshare, appearing like a flame of fire on the sacrificial ground.
verses.43: This one, named Vedavati, was previously in the Krita Yuga, and upon the arrival of the Treta Yuga, she appeared for the purpose of killing that demon.
